msgs: 52 laps, 59 passes on track and 1 safety car and 2 virtual safety cars

a: Leclerc 🏆
Ferrari, from P2 on the grid

asks.q: was it actually good or are you being nice
a: you tell me lol
59 passes on track, not counting the ones in the pit lane

asks.q: i know nothing about f1, start there
a: ok so 22 cars, lined up roughly in qualifying order, less any grid penalties
in a dry race everyone has to use two different tyre types, so everyone stops at least once, and you spend about 29 seconds in the pit lane when you do
the whole sport is basically deciding WHEN to lose that time

msgs: 27 places changed hands before they even finished lap 1

asks.q: why is the start always so mad
a: cold tyres, cold brakes, full fuel tank and everybody going for the same gap
it's the only moment of the race where the whole field is that close

asks.q: does the start decide the race
a: more than anyone admits
track position is everything on most circuits, you lose places on lap 1 and you can spend a long time stuck behind someone slower

msgs: lap 26 was the busiest of the whole race

asks.q: why do they all overtake at the same time
a: 3 cars had just stopped around then
you come out on new tyres next to someone on old ones and passing gets a lot easier
yeah, only moves made on track count here
swaps in the pit lane and stuff behind the safety car are left out

msgs: fastest lap of the race went to Antonelli

a: not anymore, there's been no point for it since 2025
it's bragging rights now
honestly not sure, the data only tells me he stopped, not why
teams give the detail later, if at all
nope, not today

msgs: and the race finished behind it

asks.q: explain safety car like i'm five
a: something's on track that shouldn't be, so a road car comes out and everyone has to queue up behind it at reduced speed
if you'd built a big lead, it's gone. the guy in P2 is now right behind you

asks.q: so is pitting under it free
a: close to it. everyone's going slow so you lose way less time stopping
the catch is everyone behind you can do the same thing, and whoever doesn't follow you inherits the lead

msgs: P1 Leclerc · P2 Russell · P3 Hamilton

asks.q: was the winner just in the fastest car
a: partly, always. the median lap times are the honest read on who had the pace
the true pace card is the one i'd trust
